references.text: The original instruction from God to make tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons, now carried out in Exodus 39:27.
The list of priestly garments to be made, including the tunic, which is part of the holy equipment for Aaron and his sons.
The beginning of the chapter describing the making of the priestly garments, where the tunics are part of the complete set.
Moses dresses Aaron in the tunic during the consecration, showing the use of what was made in Exodus 39:27.
The description of the craftsmen's skill in weaving, which is the technique used to make the tunics of fine linen.
Both verses document the actual execution of the work on the holy garments within the same narrative sequence.
Fulfillment relationship: 28:4 gives God's command regarding the tunics, which 39:27 shows has been carried out.
Planning toward execution: 31:10 defines the task that 39:27 completes.
Continuous narrative: 35:19 provides the instructions leading up to the execution in 39:27.
Conclusion on obedience: 8:36 confirms that the work on the garments (including the tunics) was completed as commanded.
